gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Expressive, with letters spaced far apart, Paprika takes the stage. Paprika is best at loud, open-countered statements, while Noto Sans Syloti Nagri, a plain sans with short ascenders, is best at holding text quietly.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-syriac-weste: Modern and clean, Noto Sans Syriac Western is a sans with terminals held far from the stroke. But Paprika is commanding and expressive, so next to it the body feels like a measured reply.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Paprika's lowercase grows as large as capitals, giving the heading a shouting, expressive presence next to Noto Sans Tagbanwa's quieter curves. Page after page, its open curves keep the text moving smoothly.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Big, loud and a bit wild, Paprika meets Noto Sans Tai Le, whose strokes taper out before touching. And Noto Sans Tai Le can stay modest in size, since its minimal cap-to-lowercase step holds up without help.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Paprika sets its lowercase at near-capital scale, spacing the letters far apart for a commanding heading. Noto Sans Tai Viet, plain sans with short ascenders, brings the best quality of all: approachable ease under a loud voice.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Paprika brings commanding, expressive display letters with lowercase as big as capitals, set against the modern sans of Noto Sans Tamil. Standout here: Tamil text that looks magnified without growing.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads in a professional, neutral way, its high midline and connected counters keeping every shape open. But Paprika is the one for making a loud, expressive entrance, while the sans quietly carries the words.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Expressive and loud, Paprika makes its point with display letters whose lowercase rivals capitals. Noto Sans Tifinagh is best at the inviting part, a sans of rounded, inflated bowls that stay open.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans Tirhuta takes the quieter role. Across paragraphs, its dominant x-height and cut-back terminals keep the sans-serif text open, a steady backdrop for Paprika's commanding display letters.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Paprika's lowercase swells to capital size, loud and expressive. Noto Sans Ugaritic, a sans-serif with almost no step from lowercase up to capitals, reads approachably over page after page, with open letter mouths like unjoined chalk arcs.
